comparison: Current integrated architecture output versus previous central sculpture output

observations: The central freestanding petal mass is absent. A continuous pearlescent sheet system rises along the right-hand boundary and curves around the upper daylight opening.
The middle circulation path and large rear arched opening remain visually unobstructed; solid left walls and a distinct ceiling opening establish an architectural volume beyond the art.
Most of the right-hand interface is still a dense screen. True views through interlayer gaps are limited, and constructability or net height cannot be verified from this image.
Long directional sheets have finer visible edges and local iridescent highlights, avoiding the former dense petal bouquet.
Broad opaque-looking portions and thick-looking bases remain. Edge separation is clearer than through-layer depth; fine precision and transparency are not consistently proven.
Foreground arrival/circulation, left reception desk, right seating with small tables, and a rear open transition are visible.
Three chairs are arranged mainly in a linear sequence along the screen; a cohesive conversational waiting group is weaker than the target.
The rear opening leads to a bright planted outlook with seating. A staggered privacy entrance boundary and onward clinical operation are not clearly legible.
No double-loaded narrow corridor is prominent, but left-side repeated openings and a longitudinal desk/seating arrangement remain.
Warm white and cream architecture, neutral upholstery and local pale purple iridescence are retained. Purple cushions from the previous output are absent.
The scene is quiet and bright, but directional sun and distinct diagonal floor/chair shadows remain; fully diffused soft daylight was not achieved.
Large sheet surfaces appear partly milky/opaque and may read as a sculptural wall rather than consistently translucent architectural layers.

nextRoundIssues: Legibility of five-stage circulation and the staggered privacy threshold
Grouped commercial waiting rather than a row of separate seats
Interlayer transparency, thin bases and precise material depth
Softer daylight and reduced directional shadows
